content:
You draft referral notes that a primary care provider (PCP) sends to a specialist. The PCP will review, edit and sign your draft, so write it in the PCP's voice, ready to send.

The reader is a specialist who has never met this patient and is triaging many referrals. They need to know quickly why the patient is being sent now, what question the PCP wants answered, what has already been tried or worked up, and anything that would change how they manage the patient. Lead with that. Leave out chart content this specialist has no use for.

Your source is a structured chart extract plus whatever the PCP typed, including their answers to follow-up questions. Every clinical statement in the note must come from one of those. The extract has no free-text notes, so symptoms, examination findings, functional status and patient preferences are absent unless the PCP supplied them; do not supply them yourself. When something this specialist would expect is missing, a follow-up question was left unanswered, or two entries in the chart disagree, say so in the final section so the PCP can fill it in before sending. A note that reads complete but contains an invented detail is worse than one with a visible gap.

Give dates for results and events. For a trend, state the direction with the first and latest values and their dates rather than listing every reading.

Format: plain text with no markdown, because the draft goes into an editable text field. Put each section heading in capitals on its own line, in this order:

REASON FOR REFERRAL
CLINICAL QUESTION
RELEVANT HISTORY
CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
KEY RESULTS
WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING

If the PCP gave no clinical question, propose the one the data best supports and mark it "[suggested - confirm]". Aim for one page, roughly 250 to 400 words. Start directly with the first heading; do not add a greeting, sign-off or commentary about the draft.

<referral_request>
Referring to: Cardiology
Referral condition: Ischemic heart disease / chronic heart failure
Urgency: routine
PCP's clinical question: Does he need stress testing or repeat angiography, and should his anti-anginal therapy change?
PCP's additional notes: Reason for referral now: over the past three months he has had chest tightness when climbing two flights of stairs that settles within five minutes of rest; no pain at rest. He has not seen cardiology since his stent.
</referral_request>

<what_this_specialist_needs>
The cardiologist will want: the cardiac diagnoses with dates, prior events and interventions (MI, PCI, CABG, heart failure admissions), latest ejection fraction and cardiac imaging, current cardiac medications (antiplatelet, statin, beta blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB, diuretic) and obvious gaps in them, blood pressure and heart rate, lipid and glycemic control, renal function and potassium, recent emergency or inpatient encounters, and smoking status.
</what_this_specialist_needs>

Write the referral note.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Routine review of ischemic heart disease with a stent placed in 2022. Over the past three months he has had chest tightness on climbing two flights of stairs, settling within five minutes of rest. No pain at rest. He has not seen cardiology since his stent.

CLINICAL QUESTION
Does he need stress testing or repeat coronary angiography, and should his anti-anginal therapy change?

RELEVANT HISTORY
Ischemic heart disease recorded 2022-09-03. Abnormal cardiac imaging and coronary angiography on 2022-09-21, with PCI on 2022-09-24. Stent details are not in the record. No MI, CABG or heart failure admission recorded. Hypertension since 1998 and hyperlipidemia since 2010. Kidney dialysis 2021-03-22 to 2023-09-04, then kidney transplant 2023-08-14. Never smoker (2026-07-06).

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
Cardiac: metoprolol succinate 100 mg ER (since 2022-09-10); clopidogrel 75 mg (since 2022-09-10); nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray (since 2022-09-10); simvastatin 20 mg (since 2022-09-10) and simvastatin 10 mg (since 2025-12-18); lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 2.5 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg (all since 2026-07-06, for hypertension).
Other: tacrolimus ER 1 mg (since 2026-07-06); insulin isophane/regular 70/30 (since 2026-07-06); tramadol 50 mg (since 2026-07-06).
No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
BP 107/53 mmHg and HR 68 on 2026-07-06. Systolic has ranged 92 to 107 since 2023.
LDL 113.7 mg/dL on 2025-12-18 (133.1 on 2021-12-07; 89.7 on 2024-06-24). HDL 42.1, triglycerides 187.5, total cholesterol 192.3 on 2025-12-18.
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR 124.7, potassium 4.6 on 2026-07-06. Creatinine was 3.0 on 2025-12-18.
HbA1c 4.1% on 2026-07-06.
Weight 92 kg, BMI 28.5 on 2026-07-06 (97.1 kg in 2023).
No echocardiogram, ejection fraction, stress test or other cardiac imaging recorded.
No ED, urgent care or inpatient encounters in the last 24 months.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Angiography and PCI in 2022. Current anti-anginal therapy is metoprolol and as-needed nitroglycerin; amlodipine was started 2026-07-06 for hypertension. No cardiac workup since 2022 is recorded.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Prediabetes (1992). Diabetic kidney disease, microalbuminuria and proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes (2002 to 2020). Obesity. Anemia (1995). Chronic back and neck pain. Dependent drug abuse (2018, active).

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Referral condition says chronic heart failure, but no heart failure diagnosis, ejection fraction or admission is in the record. Confirm or amend.
- Diabetes status: prediabetes is recorded, but so are type 2 diabetes kidney entries, and insulin was started for prediabetes. Clarify.
- Simvastatin 20 mg and 10 mg are both active. Confirm which he takes and the intended dose.
- No aspirin is recorded alongside clopidogrel. Confirm whether this is intentional.
- Symptom details not in the record: onset date, exertional limit, nitroglycerin use, adherence.
- Stent vessel and number, and the 2022 angiography report.
- Kidney status after the transplant, given the creatinine change from 3.0 to 1.1 between 2025-12-18 and 2026-07-06.
- Last hemoglobin was 2023. Recheck or confirm anemia status.
- Patient preferences about further testing.
